_comment: Task SD1 (2026-09-10). What each of John's Dallas photographs actually SHOWS, produced by READING every image rather than by parsing its filename — `alpha_dallas_01.png` says nothing at all, so `scripts/prepare_photos.py::caption_of` has nothing to read and A-L9's keyword path has nothing to match. `description` becomes the photograph's own caption in index.json, then `listing.photo_captions`, then `p.photoCaptions[i]` (amendment A15). `note` is the content verification's own sentence, kept as the record; the pipeline does not read it. `flags` is what it noted about identifiable content, carried into index.json so the image-identifiability work (A-IDP-1..6, its own branch) inherits the finding instead of re-reading 119 images — it decides nothing about what is DISPLAYED, and every seed still defaults to NOT SHOW (A-IDP-4, corrected by A-IDP-6). `own_business_name` and `own_street_number` are the listing's OWN fictional name and its own generated signage: these images were made for these listings, and a fictional name on a fictional listing identifies nobody (controller ruling, 2026-09-10, superseding the brief's blanket refusal). `composite` marks a multi-panel sheet, which never fills one of the design's six captioned slots. `refused` is a REASON, and a photograph carrying one is never encoded — it is recorded here rather than quietly left out of a staging folder, so the committed set is reproducible and the refusal is auditable. Two photographs of the 119 carry one, both in the Alpha folder: alpha_dallas_11_individual_images.png, whose fourth panel shows wall signage reading 'COMPASSIONATE HEARTS', which is not this hospital's own name and may be a real veterinary business; and alpha_dallas_05.png, whose subject is a monument sign reading '4140 CEDAR SPRINGS ROAD', an address that is not this listing's 18770 Preston Rd. Every OTHER street number stays encoded and flagged `own_street_number`: a number on a wall or above a door beside the listing's own fictional name is part of the same invented signage and names nobody, and the flag is there so the class can be re-cut whole if John wants it. Nothing else was refused: no image in the eleven folders carries a legible licence plate or an identifiable face, both checked by eye on the images the verification named.

alpha_dallas_05.png.refused: A location claim that is false. The whole subject of the largest panel is a monument sign reading '4140 CEDAR SPRINGS ROAD' — a specific, real-looking Dallas address that is NOT this listing's. Alpha is at 18770 Preston Rd. A buyer reading that photograph is told, as plainly as an image can tell them anything, that the practice is somewhere it is not, and 4140 Cedar Springs Road is a real place with a real occupant. Controller ruling, 2026-09-10, on the case rule 3's wording did not reach: the distinction from the street numbers that ARE encoded is that those are incidental to a sign about the BUSINESS (its own fictional name above its own door), and this is a sign about an ADDRESS and nothing else.

One panel of this four-panel sheet shows building signage reading 'COMPASSIONATE HEARTS' (cropped at the right edge), which is not this hospital's own fictional name and may be a real veterinary business. Checked by eye by the implementer, 2026-09-10, not taken from the verification's note alone. Everything else the sheet shows — parking, waiting room, a doorway — is unremarkable, and the cars in it carry no legible plate; the wall text alone is why it is out.
